question: What Bolinao fishery evidence does the 2018-2020 landing survey report, and what is still needed before any species or site claims can enter the public explorer?

method.summary: Reviewed the SEAFDEC/TD institutional repository record, the complete nine-page NFRDI/SEAFDEC report, and its printed reuse notice. The PDF was read online; no local copy, figure extraction, raw landing table, or complete species list was retained.
method.studyPeriodFinding: The report covers a fisheries landing survey in 2018-2020 and was published in September 2022. These are kept as separate observation and publication periods.
method.surveyFinding: Technical enumerators monitored commercial and municipal landing centers associated with four named Bolinao fishing grounds: West Philippine Sea, Bolinao coastal waters, Caquiputan Channel, and Bolinao municipal waters. The methods describe sampling every other two days and 20 sampling days per month, with raw data submitted to the NSAP database. The report notes limited months of data for Caquiputan Channel and Bolinao municipal waters, exceptionally high purse-seine landings from only two months in 2018 requiring validation, and disrupted 2020 coverage during COVID-19 restrictions.
method.rightsFinding: The report states that whole or partial reproduction in any form is allowed for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement; resale or other commercial use requires prior written permission from the SEAFDEC Secretary-General. Bangwit's eligibility for that conditional permission is not established here, so no app publication approval is inferred.

reuse.licenseAsPrinted: The publication may be reproduced in whole or in part and in any form for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement. Resale or any other commercial purpose requires prior written permission.
reuse.reason: The conditional non-commercial educational/non-profit permission does not establish that Bangwit's public app projection qualifies; no written permission for app use was sought or received.

internalConsistency.issue: The report calls the total 220 metric tonnes while its four displayed ground amounts sum to 220.1 metric tonnes.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve the source values and treat the difference as rounding or reporting precision; do not recompute a replacement total.

internalConsistency.issue: The report says 176 species types were recorded but the reviewed text does not provide a complete machine-readable 176-name list. It gives only selected leading names in prose and figures.
internalConsistency.disposition: Record the aggregate as a source claim and preserve only the explicitly readable names listed in the review; do not infer the other names or call these seven a checklist.

internalConsistency.issue: The report's stated broad group shares are approximate and sum to more than 100 percent as printed.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not treat group percentages as a mutually exclusive partition or use them as validated ecological composition.

internalConsistency.issue: Bolinao municipal waters contribute only 0.1 metric tonnes in the reported aggregate and the report says data coverage there was limited; no species-by-ground breakdown is supplied for that label.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not transfer municipality-level or other-ground species claims to the municipal-waters label.

internalConsistency.issue: The source is a landing and effort survey, not a voucher-backed biodiversity occurrence inventory; the reviewed material gives no event coordinates, specimen accessions, or species-by-individual catch dates.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep as historical catch-composition context only; do not infer current presence, exact capture locations, abundance, catchability, rules, or safety.

interpretation: This report is a useful, recent-for-Region-I historical marine fisheries source, but it describes landed catch rather than a complete biological inventory. Its 176-species aggregate is not a 176-name checklist.

The source explicitly distinguishes Bolinao coastal waters, West Philippine Sea, Caquiputan Channel, and Bolinao municipal waters. Keep those exact reported labels separate; the report does not supply reusable boundary geometry or per-species records for every ground.

Seven scientific-name strings are explicitly reported for Bolinao in the reviewed text. Their source labels have not been independently taxonomically checked, and no individual organism is confirmed by a voucher in this review.

The noncommercial educational/non-profit reproduction permission is conditional. Until Bangwit's use is shown to qualify or written permission is obtained, keep the report and its derived species claims research-only.
No raw landings, figure, map, image, geometry, species assertion, occurrence row, or public-app projection was added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.
nextAction: Continue Region I discovery across Pangasinan inland waters and estuaries, and cross-check the seven Bolinao source-name strings against authoritative fish taxonomy before considering any reuse. Seek site-resolved, reusable catch or occurrence data; keep the 176 aggregate out of a species checklist.
